title: IMF flags risks to global economy from AI market correction, war and debt
source_used: CGTN (own report of the IMF World Economic Outlook); the Reuters page returns HTTP 401
key_facts: The IMF released its latest World Economic Outlook on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 during its meetings with the World Bank in Bangkok.
Main risks named: growing debt, a prolonged Middle East conflict and the potential end of the AI investment boom.
Baseline assumes the Strait of Hormuz reopens by March 2027 and AI investment stays strong: global growth 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027.
A more protracted Middle East war could keep oil above $130 through the first quarter of 2027 and cut 2027 growth by half a percentage point.
A steep drop in AI investment could sharply cut asset prices, ultimately lowering US GDP by 1.8% and global output by 1.1% by 2028.
Petya Koeva-Brooks, deputy director of the IMF's Research Department, said resilience 'may be reaching its limits'; the AI boom is lifting only a relatively small number of countries.
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has called the US 'an economy that is standing on one leg, the AI leg'.
quote_evidence: The report also says a steep drop in AI investment could lead to a sharp drop in asset prices, ultimately cutting US GDP by 1.8% and global output by 1.1% by 2028.
On the assumption that the Strait of Hormuz reopens by next March and AI investment remains strong, the IMF predicts global growth at 3.1% for 2026 and 3.4% in 2027.

The report, released during a meeting of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, highlights growing debt levels, a prolonged Middle East conflict and the potential end of the AI investment boom as the main risks to the global economy.
why_it_matters_hint: The IMF says AI investment is propping up growth and quantifies what a sharp fall in it would cost.
notes: Reuters page returned HTTP 401. CGTN wrote its own report (with an interview) on the World Economic Outlook, so CGTN is credited, not Reuters. The Reuters analysis of the same day (C07-01) quotes the IMF's financial stability report warning that the consequences of an AI correction could be global. Our 12 Oct 2026 edition carried Georgieva's Bangkok speech and the date of this outlook. CGTN is China's state broadcaster; the figures are the Fund's.
